title: Robust FP8 Onramp: E4M3/E5M2 Stability Safeguards & Calibration Gating
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Enable FP8 (E4M3/E5M2) quantization profiles on Hopper GPUs with automated calibration gating, safety heuristics, and a production-ready rollback/fallback strategy. This ticket collects the engineering work to build a conservative onramp: calibration runner, canary gate, telemetry alerts for accuracy drift, and an automated fallback to INT8 or FP16 when safety thresholds are exceeded.

Background: Prior experiments show FP8 yields 1.8–3x throughput improvements on target models but exhibits sensitivity on narrow-precision layers and long-context workloads. We need a deployment path that minimizes customer regressions while allowing incremental rollouts. Existing artifacts: internal calibration harness (Drive: https://drive.redwood/quant/calibration-harness), perf bench (https://grafana.redwood/runtime/fp8-bench), and model compatibility matrix (internal doc).

Acceptance criteria:
- E4M3 and E5M2 profiles can be selected per-model behind a runtime feature flag and can be toggled per-route in the console.
- Canary: FP8 enabled for 2% of traffic for 72 hours with no statistically significant degradation on the golden prompt set (significance target: p>0.05) and end-to-end latency increase < 10% compared to baseline.
- Calibration runner produces a nightly profile artifact and drift delta; when nightly delta exceeds thresholds (accuracy_loss > 0.8% OR token-level perplexity increase > 1.2%), the new profile is automatically quarantined and engineers are paged.
- Automated fallback: at request time, if per-request diagnostics or shard-level telemetry indicate instability (examples: KV-cache mismatch rate > 0.2% or layer-scale spikes), the system will fall back to the last-known-good INT8 profile with a documented 99th-percentile latency budget of +200ms.
- Telemetry: add new metrics (fp8.activate_rate, fp8.drift_score, fp8.fallback_count, fp8.layer_spike_rate) and corresponding Grafana dashboards and alerting rules.

Proposed implementation plan:
1) Calibration runner: extend existing harness to produce a signed profile artifact, include per-layer sensitivity scores and per-seed stats (task-level accuracy, token-PPL). Output stored in S3 path namespaced by model-version and date. Link: https://drive.redwood/quant/calibration-spec.md
2) Canary gating: implement gating policy in routing layer to route a weighted percentage of traffic to fp8 profiles, with canary controller that evaluates golden set results and telemetry signals. Canary controller posts results to a central canary-dashboard and triggers rollback when thresholds tripped.
3) Runtime guards: lightweight per-shard heuristics (hysteresis, streak counters) to avoid flapping; incorporate temporal hysteresis of 10 minutes before deactivating FP8 on a shard.
4) Fallback flow: in-runtime fast-path to swap to INT8/FP16 for a request when diagnostics fail; emit a compact event for postmortem evaluation.
5) Nightly drift pipeline: run nightly calibration on seeded corpus, compute drift_score, surface to SRE/Model Ops Slack channel and to a dedicated dashboard.
6) Observability: add metrics and traces; ensure token-level sampling of golden set outputs for accuracy checks.

Tasks (owners):
- ENG: calibration runner extension + artifact signer (Diego)
- ENG: canary controller and dashboard (Priya Patel)
- ENG: runtime guards + fallback fast-path (Liam O'Connor)
- SRE: alerting rules and oncall playbook (Marcus Li)
- QE: golden set automation and significance tests (Sara Nguyen)

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Sensitivity thresholds: conservative thresholds reduce rollout velocity but limit customer exposure. Proposed to start conservative and relax after 4 successful canaries.
- Fallback latency acceptance: adding a quick fallback introduces small latency but preserves correctness. Targets set to +200ms for 99p to balance UX vs safety.
- Artifact signing: do we need HSM-backed signing for profile artifacts for Private customers? For now use KMS-signed artifacts; escalate if compliance asks.

Rollout plan:
- Stage 1 (internal): shadow mode for 1 week, collect telemetry, no traffic routing.
- Stage 2 (canary): 2% traffic for 72h; manual review of golden set and telemetry after 72h.
- Stage 3 (ramp): 10% -> 50% over 2 weeks with automated gate checks at each step.
- Stage 4 (GA): enable as opt-in profile in Console and API with explicit release notes.

Rollback plan:
- Immediate: canary controller flips routing back to baseline profiles and triggers diagnostic job.
- Recovery: if rollback occurs, we blacklist the specific profile artifact, trigger forced-nightly recalibration with expanded seeds, and create a postmortem with required mitigations.

rollback_plan: Canary controller flips routing, blacklists offending artifact, triggers forced nightly recalibration with expanded seeds, and creates a postmortem. If rollback triggers >3 times in 30 days, block FP8 GA for the model family until manual signoff.
notes: Conservative approach: start with shadow and small canaries. Private customers will remain opt-out until artifact signing / KMS HSM conversation resolved.
